interface.name: wp_content_frame_rate_manager_v1
interface.description:
This interface allows a client to describe the intended content frame rate of a surface so that compositors can optimize presentation timing.
A compositor generally cannot tell the cadence content is authored at from the rate at which a client happens to commit buffers. Knowing the intended cadence lets the compositor pace scanout to match it, for example by picking an output refresh rate that is an integer multiple of the content frame rate, or by applying low framerate compensation when the content rate falls below the minimum refresh rate of a variable refresh rate output. Without this information, fixed cadence content such as 23.976 fps video can be presented with an uneven distribution of frame durations, which is visible as judder.
The content frame rate is a hint and does not guarantee an exact output refresh rate or compositor behavior.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the testing phase. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can only be done by creating a new major version of the extension.

request.name: destroy

description.summary: destroy the content frame rate manager object

request.description: Destroy the content frame rate manager. This doesn't destroy objects created with the manager.

entry.name: already_constructed
entry.summary: wl_surface already has a frame rate object

request.name: get_surface_content_frame_rate

description.summary: create a new content frame rate object

request.description:
Create a new content frame rate object associated with the given surface.
Creating a wp_content_frame_rate_v1 from a wl_surface which already has one attached is a client error: already_constructed.

interface.name: wp_content_frame_rate_v1

description.summary: content frame rate object for a surface

interface.description:
The content frame rate object allows clients to hint the intended frame production cadence of content shown on a surface.
Values are represented as a rational number (numerator / denominator) to express exact rates like 24000/1001.
The client may request to switch to another frame rate at any time. When the associated surface gets destroyed, this object becomes inert and the client should destroy it.
This interface carries information in one direction only. The compositor does not report back whether or how the hint was taken into account. Clients that need to know how their content is actually being presented should use the presentation-time protocol, which reports the presentation timestamps and refresh interval that were actually used.

request.name: destroy

description.summary: destroy the content frame rate object

request.description: Switch back to not specifying any content frame rate for this surface. This is equivalent to setting the frame rate to unknown, including double-buffering semantics. See set_frame_rate for details.

request.name: set_frame_rate

description.summary: specify the surface content frame rate

request.description:
Set the content frame rate hint for the surface.
The rate is a rational value defined as numerator / denominator in frames per second. For example: - 24/1 for 24.000 fps - 24000/1001 for ~23.976 fps - 60000/1001 for ~59.94 fps
If numerator is zero, the client indicates that no specific frame rate hint applies (unknown).
A denominator of zero is invalid and is a client error: invalid_denominator.
This is purely a hint for the compositor, which may use it to choose presentation strategies such as refresh rate selection or frame pacing.
The frame rate is double-buffered state, see wl_surface.commit for details.

arg.name: numerator
arg.summary: frame rate numerator, or 0 for unknown

arg.name: denominator
arg.summary: frame rate denominator, must not be zero when numerator is non-zero
